interest: Japanese naval visits to the Philippines in the 1930s.
overview: This file comprises the Department of State's official docket registry sheets ('List of Papers', Form DS-46) for decimal file 894.3311B (and 894.3311), recording correspondence and official actions from 1931 to 1939 regarding visits of Imperial Japanese naval vessels and auxiliaries to ports in the Philippine Islands, with occasional calls at Honolulu, Hawaii. The documents indexed include notes from the Japanese Embassy in Washington requesting permission, courtesies, and replenishment facilities (fuel, food, and water) for training squadrons, cruisers, transports, and minelayers—including the Yahagi, Yakumo, Idzumo, Iwate, Asama, Kuma, Tatsuta, Ondo, Sata, Yubari, Erimo, Sunosaki, Okinoshima, Tsurumi, and Shiriya—calling at Manila, Davao, Iloilo, Zamboanga, and Cebu. The entries document interdepartmental coordination among the State Department (Divisions of Far Eastern Affairs and Protocol), the War Department (Bureau of Insular Affairs and the Commanding General, Philippine Department), the Navy Department (Chief of Naval Operations and naval authorities in Manila), and the Governor General and later U.S. High Commissioner to the Philippine Islands, addressing quarantine reroutings, itinerary changes, inspections of Cavite Naval Base, and reciprocal treatment of naval vessels.

subfiles.about: Department of State List of Papers indexing correspondence and actions regarding visits of Japanese naval vessels and aircraft to Philippine ports from 1931 to 1939.
subfiles.summary: This multi-page administrative docket list (Form DS-46) records incoming and outgoing correspondence concerning proposed visits of Imperial Japanese naval vessels and auxiliary ships to the Philippine Islands between 1931 and 1939. Entries document formal notifications and requests from the Japanese Embassy in Washington for port courtesies and replenishment facilities for training squadrons, cruisers, oilers, transports, and minelayers visiting ports such as Manila, Davao, Iloilo, Zamboanga, and Cebu, as well as Honolulu. The register details internal routing and clearance procedures between the State Department's Division of Far Eastern Affairs and Division of Protocol, the War Department's Bureau of Insular Affairs, the Commanding General of the Philippine Department, the U.S. Navy Department, and the U.S. High Commissioner to the Philippines. Notable entries address adjustments for cholera outbreaks, visits to the U.S. Naval Base at Cavite, and policy discussions on reciprocity and avoiding discrimination against Japanese vessels.
